html:
The Baptist War was a rising of some sixty thousand enslaved people in western Jamaica that began at Christmas 1831. Its leader was Samuel Sharpe, a Baptist deacon.

Sharpe planned a peaceful strike: the enslaved would refuse to work until paid wages. It turned into a revolt in which estates were burned. Troops put it down within weeks, and hundreds of rebels were killed or hanged, Sharpe among them in 1832.

Planters blamed missionaries and wrecked chapels. But reports of the revolt and the killings in its wake shocked the British public, and Parliament passed the Slavery Abolition Act in 1833. Sharpe is a National Hero of Jamaica.
sum: The Baptist War was a rising of some sixty thousand enslaved people in western Jamaica that began at Christmas 1831. Its leader was Samuel Sharpe, a Baptist deacon.
